printed 'ἀκανδώδης', correct 'ἀκανθώδης'. From ἄκανθα: ἀκανθώδης. The line above prints ἀκανθώδης with a crossed θ, and this one a triangular δ — the same word, two sorts. The text keeps the ink; work/corrigenda/entries.json carries the fix.

rulings.note: John 2026-08-13, carried 2026-08-18 to 28 sites a Latin Z still held (AZι 24, AZγ 2, KaZμ 2 — Karsch keyed like Aubert-Wimmer) plus page-094-L:21 where the A itself was a Greek alpha. The discriminator is the NEXT character: a Latin Z before a Greek letter is a work siglum; before anything else it is Zeller, Zeitschr, Ztschr or a Homeric book letter and is left alone.

John from the review page; was ἀγνός. Rough breathing — `ἁγνὲ` on line 55 is the same word with rough three lines down. He typed the omicron as U+1F40 (with psili); read as a slip, since a breathing cannot stand mid-word, so the acute is kept.

John from the review page: "it's δεῖ"; was ἀεῖ. Neither card option was the ink — the sweeps offered ἀεὶ/ἀεῖ and both misread the delta. Crop verified anchored: followed by `Vhl Rh`, matching the corpus `ἀεῖ Vhl Rhet`. ἀεῖ was a hapax across 176 columns.

John from the review page: "δῖαν"; was ὀῖαν. None of the three card options was the ink — οἷαν/ὀίαν/ὀῖαν all read the delta as an omicron. `αἰθέρα δῖαν (Emp 379)` is Empedocles' divine aether, and δῖαν is the feminine accusative of δῖος. Second delta-for-omicron misread of the day; cf page-023-L:51 ἀεῖ->δεῖ.

John: "ματος (final sigma, obviously second part of a hyphenated column break word)". The line-end hyphen was LOST in reconciliation — raw/opus reads `ἐξ αἵ-` and the corpus read `ἐξ αἵ`. Without it merge_review could not join the word, smyth E1 flagged the tail `ματος` as an accentless word, and the card then offered to make its final sigma a stigma numeral. Restored. Checked corpus-wide against Opus: this is the ONLY line where a hyphen went missing, and none was invented.

John: the uneven printing "suggested a space that shouldn't be there". Corpus read `καλȣ μεν`; the ink reads καλȣ͂μεν as one word with the circumflex on the ȣ (καλοῦμεν). Space closed and the circumflex written. The spurious space is what made smyth E1 flag `μεν` as a word with no accent.

John from the review page: "ὡς"; the corpus read ὑς (upsilon with dasia). Neither card option was the ink — it offered `ύς` and a stigma variant of it, both upsilon. `γενόμενον ἴσμεν ὡς τῷ ἐνεργεῖν` is the idiom; ὑς ("pig") is nonsense there. Third letter-level misread of the sitting, after 023-L:51 ἀεῖ->δεῖ and 027-R:10 ὀῖαν->δῖαν — in each the sweeps agreed on a wrong letter and only the ink settled it.

John from the review page: "ἁλῴη"; corpus read ἀλῴῃ. Two changes in one: the breathing goes smooth->rough, and the SECOND iota subscript comes off the eta — the corpus carried one under the ω and another under the η, the ink has only the ω. `ἄστυ ἁλῴη (Hom Ι 592)`. The card offered ἀλώη/ἁλώη, neither of which shows a subscript at all, so it could not have been answered from the buttons.

John: "da hell opus?" — the corpus held ȣ + U+0314 ROUGH + U+0342 PERISPOMENI + U+0314 ROUGH AGAIN. The duplicate breathing is a keystroke, not a reading of the ink: the crop shows one rough and one circumflex, and the sense (οὗ αἴτιον τὸ αἴτιον, Φβ3. 195b7) requires οὗ. This was the ONLY site in 176 columns where two breathings stood on one letter — smyth A5 and A9 both caught it, and both were right.

John: "φτα5. 820b5. looks lowercase to me" — and it is. The corpus held the ONLY capital Φτα against 52 lowercase φτ sigla, and `φτα5. 820` occurs three more times lowercase with the identical chapter and Bekker page. φτ is περὶ Φυτῶν, 815-830, and every occurrence falls inside it. This also dissolves the siglum sweep's complaint: it read the capital as Φ = Φυσικὴ ἀκρόασις (184-267) and objected that 820 lies outside. The work was never Physics — the case of the letter IS the siglum.

rulings.note: John from the follow-up page: "headword is ROUGH". I had argued the other way from LSJ — the halcyon has no tie to ἅλς and the lexicon prints ἀλκυών smooth — but the ink is what governs and Bonitz sets rough. So the four rough inflections were RIGHT and the headword was the odd one; my reading of the family split was backwards.

John from the follow-up page: "headword is rough and so is this". Second entry in a row where the corpus held a SMOOTH headword over rough inflections and the ink has rough — cf page-045-L:27 ἀλκυών->ἁλκυών minutes earlier. This supersedes his own `forms:ἀδρός|ἁδρός -> preserve ἀδρός` from the same day: that card showed the form without its entry, and the headword read against the inflections is what settled it.

John from the follow-up page: "ἀλεὠρα" — omega, not upsilon. The entry headword on l.34 IS `ἀλεώρα` and its own gloss reads "Bk modo ἀλεώρα exhibet, modo ἀλεωρά, modo ἀλεωρή", so the word was never ἄλευρα (flour) at all. The card offered ἀλεύρα/ἄλευρα, neither of which is the word — my note about a feminine article not fitting a neuter plural was right about the grammar and wrong about which lemma this is.

John from the follow-up page. Line 50 opens `ἐστιν` — an ENCLITIC — so this is Smyth §183b: proparoxytone ἄλυτον takes an additional acute on the ultima. The corpus had the enclitic's acute and was MISSING the word's own accent on the alpha. Line 50 also prints plain `ἄλυτον` with nothing following it, which settles where the lemma's accent sits. Neither card option was right: it offered ἀλυτόν and ἄλυτον, one accent each.

John from the follow-up page: "ἀκρώτη-". The ω carries the accent and the η carries none. ⚠ MY CARD SAID "THREE ACCENTS" AND THAT WAS WRONG: line 33 opens `ριόν τι`, and `τι` is an enclitic, so the acute on the ultima is Smyth §183b and correct. Two accents, not three — the word's own, misplaced onto the ω where Greek puts it on the η (ἀκρωτήριον), plus the enclitic's. A compositor's slip, kept as printed. Neither card option was the ink: they offered ἀκρωτή- and ἀκρώτή-.

John from the follow-up page: "661a10" — no mark between the page and the column letter. The corpus writes this shape 5,904 times (3,960 as NNNaL, 1,944 as NNN aL) and punctuated it only three times; this very line already prints `660a17` clean five words earlier. The comma was a speck read as type.
